## Code

Standalone R scripts, for slides that have one, and a starting template for your own documents.

- [`predictionOLS26.R`](https://github.com/clavedark/MLEfall26/blob/main/predictionOLS26.R) — R script from the linear model prediction slides.
- [`binarymodels26.R`](https://github.com/clavedark/MLEfall26/blob/main/binarymodels26.R) — R script from the binary models slides. Reads `dp.dta`, below.
- [`avg-preds-step-by-step.R`](https://github.com/clavedark/MLEfall26/blob/main/avg-preds-step-by-step.R) — average effects for the Exercise #5 hazard model, built one step at a time: one leader-year, then three, then the whole sample, then every year of tenure at three Polity values, with delta-method and simulated intervals. It is Part III of the Exercise #5 answer key as a plain script. Reads Archigos from the web and Polity V from `data/p5v2018.csv` — see [Polity V](#data) below for where to get it. Click **Download raw file**.
- [`pdftemplate26.qmd`](https://github.com/clavedark/MLEfall26/blob/main/pdftemplate26.qmd) — a short Quarto starter that renders to PDF, for exercise write-ups and for papers. Copy it, rename it, and write over the placeholder sections. It needs no data, so rendering it unchanged is a quick way to find out whether your machine is set up. Instructions are in the comment block at the top, including what to change for a paper and how to produce a PDF without installing LaTeX. Click **Download raw file**.

## Data

- [CES 2020 (`ces.csv`)](https://github.com/clavedark/MLEfall26/blob/main/data/ces.csv) — individual-level responses from the 2020 *Cooperative Election Study*, reached through the "American Voter Bot" project; used in exercises #1 and #2. GitHub won't preview a file this size — click **Download raw file**. Variable descriptions are in the [codebook](cescodebook26.qmd).
  *Source: Cooperative Election Study, Harvard University. [CES project site](https://cces.gov.harvard.edu).*
- [Democratic peace (`dp.dta`)](https://github.com/clavedark/MLEfall26/blob/main/data/dp.dta) — dyad-year data, 1951–1985, 20,990 rows: militarized dispute onset (`dispute`) with a shared border, the capability ratio, the lower of the two Polity scores (`deml`), an alliance indicator, and joint IGO memberships. Used in the binary models, likelihood, and maximization slides. Stata format — read it with `haven::read_dta()`. Click **Download raw file**.
  *Source: Oneal, John R., and Bruce M. Russett. 1997. "The Classic Liberals Were Right: Democracy, Interdependence, and Conflict, 1950-1985." International Studies Quarterly 41(2): 267-294.*
- [ITT data (`ITT.csv`)](https://github.com/clavedark/MLEfall26/blob/main/data/ITT.csv) — Ill-Treatment and Torture allegation counts by country-year, merged with World Bank (WDI) and Polity covariates; used in the `predictionOLS.R` script.
  *Source: Conrad, Courtenay R., Jillienne Haglund, and Will H. Moore. 2013. "Disaggregating Torture Allegations: Introducing the Ill-Treatment and Torture (ITT) Country-Year Data." International Studies Perspectives 14(2): 199-220. [ITT project page](https://faculty.ucmerced.edu/cconrad2/Academic/ITT_Data_Collection.html).*
- [Leader-years (`leaderyears.csv`)](https://github.com/clavedark/MLEfall26/blob/main/data/leaderyears.csv) — 17,686 leader-years, 1840–2015: one row per year a leader held office, with how the spell ended, how the leader took power, gender, year of birth, and a five-way regional grouping cut from the country codes. Reshaped from Archigos 4.1. Used in exercise #4. Click **Download raw file**.
  *Source: Goemans, Henk E., Kristian Skrede Gleditsch, and Giacomo Chiozza. 2009. "Introducing Archigos: A Dataset of Political Leaders." Journal of Peace Research 46(2): 269-283. [Archigos data page](https://www.rochester.edu/college/faculty/hgoemans/data.htm).*
- [Polity V (`p5v2018.xls`)](https://www.systemicpeace.org/inscr/p5v2018.xls) — country-year regime scores, including the combined `polity2` score (−10 to +10) used in exercise #5 and in the discrete hazards slides. Not posted here: the Center for Systemic Peace does not allow redistribution without its written permission, so download it from their [data page](https://www.systemicpeace.org/inscrdata.html) — Excel format — and save it as a CSV named `p5v2018.csv` in your `data/` folder, which is where the scripts look for it. Variable definitions are in the [Polity5 users' manual](https://www.systemicpeace.org/inscr/p5manualv2018.pdf).
  *Source: Marshall, Monty G., and Ted Robert Gurr. 2020. "Polity5: Political Regime Characteristics and Transitions, 1800–2018. Dataset Users' Manual." Center for Systemic Peace. [Polity project page](https://www.systemicpeace.org/inscrdata.html).*
